reasoning_traces.think:
The Murphy decomposition separates Brier score into three orthogonal components: reliability (REL), resolution (RES), and uncertainty (UNC). REL measures how well predicted probabilities match empirical frequencies; RES quantifies the ability to distinguish outcome classes; UNC reflects base-rate dominance. The identity Brier ≈ REL - RES + UNC reveals that improving calibration requires reducing REL while increasing RES, subject to bounded UNC. In practice, RES near zero indicates insufficient discrimination, whereas moderate REL suggests miscalibration. The codebase enforces these metrics through brierDecomposition and murphy-components-explore modules, ensuring that calibration diagnostics remain grounded in empirical observables rather than speculative models.
